title: Long SMH — AI Semis Read-Through (Lower-Beta NVDA Expression)
entry: Thursday open, first 30-min consolidation. Do NOT chase if SMH opens up more than 4%. Patient entry: pullback to $530-$535 within first hour of trading.
stop_loss: $510 daily close (~5% below entry, aligns with NVDA $215 invalidation)
catalyst: NVDA's $91B Q2 guide is a direct read-through for the AI semi stack — AMD, TSM, AVGO, MU all supply the same data center build-out. SMH lagged NVDA into earnings; the sector ETF is the cleaner expression with less single-stock post-earnings noise.
thesis: SMH is the lower-beta way to own the AI capex confirmation trade. The 25-stock semi basket smooths out single-name volatility — you skip the 'beats and drops' reflex that hits NVDA individually. Heavy NVDA weight (~22%) gives you the upside; AMD, TSM, AVGO, MU, ASML diversify the entry point. The ETF underperformed NVDA going into earnings — about 8 points of relative underperformance over 30 days — which means it has room to catch up if the AI capex thesis holds. Particularly attractive if NVDA gaps too hard at open: SMH lets you participate without paying the gap premium. Memory cycle (MU/HBM) and EUV (ASML) get pulled along too, both of which had earnings tailwinds NVDA can't capture.
bull_case: AI capex confirmed across the basket — Q2 earnings season (AMD, MU, AVGO reporting late May/early June) all benefit from NVDA's $91B guide as a demand-confirmation signal. SMH breaks above $555 within 2 weeks, $575 by mid-June. Structural Rubin platform announcement drives sector re-rating; ASML EUV monopoly stays intact.
bear_case: AI capex paradoxically benefits NVDA at the expense of the broader basket — hyperscalers consolidate spend on NVDA Blackwell/Rubin and cut second-source orders to AMD/TSM. SMH lags NVDA materially through the rotation. If NVDA stops out at $215, SMH likely trades to $510-$515 (correlation 0.85+).
invalidation: Daily close below $510, OR NVDA breaks $215 (whichever first)

sources.label: NVDA Q2 guide drives semi sector — TradingKey

outcome.note: SMH rallied strongly on NVDA's $91B Q2 guide read-through, surging 3.28% to $564.66 on the session. First target of $555 was cleared on the open gap and held through the day. Entry condition (patient pullback to $530-535) was not met — the ETF gapped too far at open — but the $555 target level was decisively achieved. Price at target: $555; session high $564.66 per Yahoo Finance.
